 A workspace, like a jacket, should be tailored —
 and here the tailor is your own two hands.

 S2:
 prefix z — and a pane swallows the window whole.
 One moment you had four rooms and a chorus,
 the next, a single cathedral of the current task.
 The others did not die; they waited, folded,
 like clothes in a drawer, like books on shelves.
 Press z again and the whole arrangement
 snaps back into being, unsnapped, restored.
 Zoom is the art of leaving without leaving,
 the way a reader lifts a page to better light
 and knows exactly where to put it back.

 S3:
 There are days one pane deserves its own window.
 break-pane, the letter b, evicts the cell
 into its own room; join-pane invites it back,
 anywhere, any arrangement, any window —
 a pane is a citizen, movable by law,
 residing wherever you decree tomorrow.
 swap-pane trades two cells across the border,
 left window trading right. The walls are soft
 here, or rather the walls are nothing, only
 habits, and habits are freely editable.

 S4:
 Learn display-panes — q — the brief numbers
 that bloom in every cell when called.
 Not just navigation: a census, a roll call
 of everything currently running on your behalf —
 htop counting cores, tail guarding a log,
 a
